description.value: The study examined neural responses to social inclusion, exclusion, and passive watching in females with borderline personality disorder, major depressive disorder, and healthy controls, focusing on group differences in inclusion-related activation and its relationship with borderline symptom severity.

spans.text: To examine social interactions under laboratory settings during fMRI and to warrant comparability with previous investigations, we used the well-established “cyberball” paradigm ( 20 ).

design.value: A 3 × 3 group-by-condition fMRI design compared healthy controls, borderline personality disorder, and major depressive disorder across passive watching, inclusion, and exclusion conditions, with post-hoc differential contrasts and within-BPD correlation analyses.

spans.text: For second level group analyses, we computed a 3 × 3 ANOVA model (omnibus F -test) with the two factors “group” (HC, BPD, MD) and “condition” (passive watching, inclusion, exclusion)
